narrative_sections.enterprise_brief_title: An Integrated Care & Health-Plan Enterprise Building the Governed Foundation for AI at Scale
narrative_sections.enterprise_brief_summary:
Meridian Health System runs a $650M FY26 IT budget at a 75/25 run/change posture, with 12 approved programs and 12 candidate AI opportunities. The evidence base is broad, but value realization is still gated by baseline, ownership, and finance-validation maturity.

The current technology estate is substantial rather than thin: Epic Hyperspace, Clarity, and Caboodle anchor clinical operations; SQL Server reporting marts, Tableau, Power BI, and SAS carry fragmented analytics demand; and AWS plus Databricks is the target direction, not a certified current-state platform.

The strategic implication is clear: Meridian should fund the governed lakehouse, semantic layer, identity spine, and data-governance operating model before treating individual AI use cases as ready-to-scale investments.
narrative_sections.enterprise_hero_summary: Meridian Health System is an integrated delivery network and health plan headquartered in Sacramento, CA with $16.8B revenue and 58,000 employees. Its model spans hospitals, ambulatory clinics, health-plan operations, pharmacy, contact center, finance, and analytics modernization.

gaps.title: No certified medallion architecture (AWS/Databricks)
gaps.blocks: Unified clinical + claims lakehouse cannot advance. No bronze/silver/gold data products are evidenced. Target state is aspirational only.

gaps.title: No formal data governance operating model
gaps.blocks: AI/LLM automation use case is not decision-grade. Blocks semantic layer certification, AI audit trail, and data quality rule enforcement across all use cases.

gaps.title: No certified semantic layer
gaps.blocks: AI/LLM, cost transparency, and automated close use cases cannot produce governed outputs. SQL Server mart sprawl creates duplicated, ungoverned business rules.

gaps.title: No patient/member identity spine loaded
gaps.blocks: Unified lakehouse and call center optimization both require a resolved member identity. Claims, pharmacy, and EMR data cannot be joined without it.

gaps.title: Provider contract terms not digitized in governed form
gaps.blocks: End-to-end cost transparency and provider quality use cases cannot produce margin or attribution outputs. Capitation and value-based contract logic remain in manual documents.

gaps.title: Transcript governance and intent taxonomy not certified
gaps.blocks: Call center optimization cannot advance to agent assist or next-best-action. Real-time CRM integration and member identity linkage are also unproven.

gaps.title: Rules and model lineage not governed; provider entity resolution unproven
gaps.blocks: Payment integrity and leakage reduction cannot quantify recoveries. SAS model lineage is ungoverned. Investigation and recovery tracking workflows are not evidenced.

gaps.title: Close workflow integration unproven; finance semantic layer not evidenced
gaps.blocks: Automated close and reporting use case cannot advance. Manual reporting maintenance load and ungoverned metric definitions prevent close-cycle acceleration.
